passages.text: Woe to those who devise iniquity and plot evil on their beds! At morning’s light they accomplish it because the power is in their hands.
passages.sermon:
God warns people who plan evil.
These people think about wickedness while they lie in bed.
They make evil plans at night.
When morning comes, they do what they planned.
They do evil because they have the power to do it.
passages.original: ה֧וֹי חֹֽשְׁבֵי־ אָ֛וֶן וּפֹ֥עֲלֵי רָ֖ע עַל־ מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם בְּא֤וֹר הַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ יַעֲשׂ֔וּהָ כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־ לְאֵ֖ל יָדָֽם׃

passages.text: They covet fields and seize them; they take away houses. They deprive a man of his home, a fellow man of his inheritance.
passages.sermon:
Wicked people desire fields that do not belong to them.
They take these fields by force.
They want houses that are not theirs.
They seize these houses from others.
They oppress a man and take away his home.
They rob another man of his inheritance.
passages.original: וְחָמְד֤וּ שָׂדוֹת֙ וְגָזָ֔לוּ וּבָתִּ֖ים וְנָשָׂ֑אוּ וְעָֽשְׁקוּ֙ גֶּ֣בֶר וּבֵית֔וֹ וְאִ֖ישׁ וְנַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “I am planning against this nation a disaster from which you cannot free your necks. Then you will not walk so proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Israel.
The LORD says, “I am planning disaster against this nation.
You will not escape this disaster.
You will not be able to free your necks from it.
You will not walk proudly anymore.
This will be a time of calamity.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י חֹשֵׁ֛ב עַל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את רָעָ֑ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ תָמִ֨ישׁוּ מִשָּׁ֜ם צַוְּארֹֽתֵיכֶ֗ם וְלֹ֤א תֵֽלְכוּ֙ רוֹמָ֔ה כִּ֛י עֵ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִֽיא׃

passages.text: In that day they will take up a proverb against you and taunt you with this bitter lamentation: ‘We are utterly ruined! He has changed the portion of my people. How He has removed it from me! He has allotted our fields to traitors.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God warns them about a coming day of judgment.
On that day, others will speak a proverb about you.
They will mock you with a bitter lament.
They will say, “We are completely ruined.”
They will say, “God has changed the share of my people.”
They will say, “God has taken my portion away from me.”
They will say, “God has given our fields to traitors.”
passages.original: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִשָּׂ֧א עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם מָשָׁ֗ל וְנָהָ֨ה נְהִ֤י נִֽהְיָה֙ אָמַר֙ שָׁד֣וֹד נְשַׁדֻּ֔נוּ חֵ֥לֶק עַמִּ֖י יָמִ֑יר אֵ֚יךְ יָמִ֣ישׁ לִ֔י לְשׁוֹבֵ֥ב שָׂדֵ֖ינוּ יְחַלֵּֽק׃

passages.text: Therefore, you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to divide the land by lot.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to this nation.
The LORD says a consequence will come.
You will not have anyone to assign land to you.
No one will divide your portion by lot.
This will happen in the assembly of the LORD.
You will lose your share among God’s people.
passages.original: לָכֵן֙ לֹֽא־ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לְךָ֔ מַשְׁלִ֥יךְ חֶ֖בֶל בְּגוֹרָ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Do not preach,” they preach. “Do not preach these things; disgrace will not overtake us.”
passages.sermon:
The people say, "Do not preach."
They command, "Do not speak these words."
They believe, "Disgrace will not come to us."
passages.original: אַל־ תַּטִּ֖פוּ יַטִּיפ֑וּן לֹֽא־ יַטִּ֣פוּ לָאֵ֔לֶּה לֹ֥א יִסַּ֖ג כְּלִמּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Should it be said, O house of Jacob, “Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient? Are these the things He does?” Do not My words bring good to him who walks uprightly?
passages.sermon:
The house of Jacob is the people of Israel.
The LORD is God.
God has a Spirit.
Some people ask about God.
They say, “Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient?”
They also say, “Are these the things God does?”
God answers them.
God says, “My words bring good.”
God’s words help the person who walks uprightly.
The upright person does what is right.
God’s words do not harm the upright person.
passages.original: הֶאָמ֣וּר בֵּֽית־ יַעֲקֹ֗ב הֲקָצַר֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה אִם־ אֵ֖לֶּה מַעֲלָלָ֑יו הֲל֤וֹא דְבָרַ֨י יֵיטִ֔יבוּ עִ֖ם הַיָּשָׁ֥ר הוֹלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: But of late My people have risen up like an enemy: You strip off the splendid robe from unsuspecting passersby like men returning from battle.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel.
Recently, His people have acted like enemies.
They attack others.
They take away splendid robes from people passing by.
These people are unsuspecting.
They are like men returning safely from battle.
God’s people strip them of their garments.
passages.original: וְאֶתְמ֗וּל עַמִּי֙ לְאוֹיֵ֣ב יְקוֹמֵ֔ם מִמּ֣וּל שַׂלְמָ֔ה אֶ֖דֶר תַּפְשִׁט֑וּן מֵעֹבְרִ֣ים בֶּ֔טַח שׁוּבֵ֖י מִלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: You drive the women of My people from their pleasant homes. You take away My blessing from their children forever.
passages.sermon: God speaks to the people of Israel.\r\nYou force the women of My people to leave their pleasant homes.\r\nYou remove My blessing from their children forever.
passages.original: נְשֵׁ֤י עַמִּי֙ תְּגָ֣רְשׁ֔וּן מִבֵּ֖ית תַּֽעֲנֻגֶ֑יהָ מֵעַל֙ עֹֽלָלֶ֔יהָ תִּקְח֥וּ הֲדָרִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Arise and depart, for this is not your place of rest, because its defilement brings destruction— a grievous destruction!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He tells them to get up.
He tells them to leave this place.
This place is not a place of rest for them.
This place is defiled.
Defilement brings destruction here.
The destruction will be severe.
passages.original: ק֣וּמוּ וּלְכ֔וּ כִּ֥י לֹא־ זֹ֖את הַמְּנוּחָ֑ה בַּעֲב֥וּר טָמְאָ֛ה תְּחַבֵּ֖ל וְחֶ֥בֶל נִמְרָֽץ׃

passages.text: If a man of wind were to come and say falsely, “I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,” he would be just the preacher for this people!
passages.sermon:
Micah speaks to the people of Israel.
He describes the people as loving falsehood.
He says, "Suppose a man comes who is full of empty words and lies."
This man says, 'I will preach to you about wine and strong drink.'
Such a man would be the right preacher for these people.
The people want to hear messages about pleasure and indulgence.
They do not want to hear the truth from God.
passages.original: לוּ־ אִ֞ישׁ הֹלֵ֥ךְ ר֙וּחַ֙ וָשֶׁ֣קֶר כִּזֵּ֔ב אַטִּ֣ף לְךָ֔ לַיַּ֖יִן וְלַשֵּׁכָ֑ר וְהָיָ֥ה מַטִּ֖יף הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will collect the remnant of Israel. I will bring them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in the midst of its pasture— a noisy throng.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jacob and Israel.
God promises to gather all of Jacob.
God will collect the remnant of Israel.
God will bring them together.
They will be like sheep gathered in a pen.
They will be like a flock in the middle of its pasture.
The people will be many and noisy.
passages.original: אָסֹ֨ף אֶאֱסֹ֜ף יַעֲקֹ֣ב כֻּלָּ֗ךְ קַבֵּ֤ץ אֲקַבֵּץ֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֥חַד אֲשִׂימֶ֖נּוּ כְּצֹ֣אן בָּצְרָ֑ה כְּעֵ֙דֶר֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַדָּֽבְר֔וֹ תְּהִימֶ֖נָה מֵאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: One who breaks open the way will go up before them; they will break through the gate, and go out by it. Their King will pass through before them, the LORD as their leader.
passages.sermon:
The LORD leads His people.
The LORD is their King.
A leader goes ahead of the people.
He breaks open the way for them.
The people follow this leader.
They break through the gate.
They go out through the gate.
Their King passes before them.
The LORD is at their head.
passages.original: עָלָ֤ה הַפֹּרֵץ֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם פָּֽרְצוּ֙ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔רוּ שַׁ֖עַר וַיֵּ֣צְאוּ ב֑וֹ וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר מַלְכָּם֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיהוָ֖ה בְּרֹאשָֽׁם׃פ
